Great to meet you yesterday. Per our kickoff, I wanted to put a compact onboarding plan in one place so your engineers and procurement have a clear checklist for the coming two weeks. High-level goals: get SDK integrated into your staging environment, validate endpoint migration path, and run a 48-hour soak in staging with realistic traffic.

Top-level plan (summary):

- Day 3–6: Stage integration + endpoint migration window (rolling switch)
- Day 7–10: Resilience testing — retries/timeouts and rate-limit tuning (we'll help tune quotas)
- Day 11–14: Sign-off & production cutover checklist

Attachments: integration checklist (PDF) and SDK sample snippets (zip).

Primary asks from your side this week:
1) Confirm staging cutover window (preferred: Tue 10/14 10:00–12:00 PT)
2) Share staging IP allowlist or VPN details for our dev instances
3) Point to the engineer who will own retries/timeouts tuning (name + email)

I'll loop in Vivek (solutions eng) for the technical snippets and Lauren (CS manager) to own the handoff cadence.

Katya — thanks for the quick read. Quick answers inline and next steps.

1) Migration approach: we generally prefer a staged proxy rewrite during the staging window. That gives you the most control and lets us fail back quickly. DNS switch with low TTL works too but requires more coordination with your infra team. Recommendation: proxy rewrite for staging test, DNS cutover for production if you want a single canonical host.

2) Endpoints & certs: attaching a short doc with the FQDNs and expected cert chain. If procurement/security require thumbprints, we can extract those and send over. (Attachment: foresight-integration-checklist.pdf)

3) Rate limits & SDK: the SDK exposes an optional client-side throttler and a retry policy object that you can configure per-route. For your nightly batch, configure the SDK to use adaptive backoff with a 5xx jitter and a max concurrency of 6 for batch endpoints. We'll send recommended default values.

Daniel — can you confirm whether your staging is behind a proxy we can rewrite (nginx/Envoy)? If so, please share the proxy config or access for one of your dev hosts.

Vivek — adding you to provide example snippets for the proxy rewrite, timeout/retry config, and a simple traffic-shaper example for their batch job.

Next steps (concrete):
- I will share a short runbook link with the exact curl commands and proxy snippet (Drive link).
- Vivek will provide Node + Python examples and a short checklist for the staging cutover.
- Katya/Daniel to confirm staging window and provide allowlist VPN/IPs.

Hi all — quick technical follow-up and practical snippets to speed the staging run. Attaching the SDK sample bundle; below are the essential pieces so your engineers can start immediately.

A. Proxy rewrite (Envoy example)
- Add a route that rewrites /api/v1/* to the Redwood staging endpoint (staging.redwood-inference.com) and preserves Host header. Example (pseudo):
  route:
    match: prefix
    rewrite:
      prefix_rewrite: "/api/v1/"
    cluster: redwood_staging

B. SDK retry/timeouts (Node example)
- Minimal pattern:
  const client = new RedwoodClient({
    timeoutMs: 8000, // per-call timeout
    retry: { attempts: 3, backoffMs: 300, maxBackoffMs: 2000, jitter: true }
  });

- For large batch job: set maxConcurrency: 6 and add an additional 30s socket timeout on the lower-level HTTP transport.

C. Rate-limit handling
- The SDK surfaces a 429 handler hook you can implement to do exponential backoff + token-bucket smoothing locally. We'll provide a small util in the zip (rate-smoother.js).

D. Validation checks (run these in staging):
1) Single-message generation smoke (10 reqs/s) — confirm latency p50/p95
2) Batch job simulation (concurrency 6, large payloads) — ensure 429s are handled and no silent cache misses
3) KV/prefix caching validation — confirm that repeated prefixes return cached tokens on subsequent requests

Notes: if you want us to onboard a temporary dedicated pool for the two-day staging soak (to remove noisy neighbor variance), we can spin up a short trial — flag and we'll request approvals.

Attachments: sdk-sample-snippets.zip (includes node/, python/, go/ examples), small traffic-shaper snippet, and a short envoy-route-example.yaml.

Happy to jump on a 30-min debug call — Mateo, if they confirm Wed 10/14 window, we can schedule a prep call Mon 10/13 09:00 PT for a quick dry run.

Vivek Kulkarni
